question: What is the meaning of tax benefits in relation to tax benefits?
description: Tax benefits refer to financial advantages or reductions in tax liabilities that can be obtained through various means, such as deductions, credits, or exemptions. In the context of sustainable construction, tax benefits can incentivize the use of environmentally friendly materials and practices, promoting the transition to more circular and sustainable building systems. This aligns with the goals of materials passports, which aim to increase the value of materials over time and reduce the eco-footprint. By leveraging tax benefits, developers, managers, and renovators can make more informed decisions about material choices, ultimately contributing to a more circular economy.

3.8. Goals 
The ’identification of reuse value in the product’ is listed as the 
primary goal of a passport. A major part of this particular goal originates 
from papers related to the BAMB research project (Debacker and 
Manshoven, 2016), but it is used also extensively in direct phrasing or 
similar wording in other projects (Bertino et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2019; 
Merrild et al., 2016; Wittenveen & Bos, 2018). Any instrument, thus also 
a passport, is of course not limited by default, to serve a single goal. 
Passport’s also frequently aim ’to stimulate reuse and recycling’ and in 
general ’support CE decision making’, either in addition to the primary 
goal or as the primary goal. The majority of identified goals relate to 
circularity, hence, makes it clearly distinctive from e.g., PLM, and 
maintenance systems. More extensive analyzed goal results can be found 
in Fig. A3 (Appendix 3.1).
